# SHEL — Shell (IDEATION 2026-11-06)

**Signal / why now:** SHEL is #11 GLOBAL MOMENTUM, $100.12, **−7.88% off its 52-week high** — the only un-carded GLOBAL row not sitting on its high (mom12 +36.2%, mom6 +21.0%, mom1 +3.4%, CAGR 26.1%, vol 22.2%, ADV $647m). The desk's macro block is where the tailwind comes from: Brent 102.70 with the war premium intact bids the energy complex.

**Regime: NEUTRAL** (not WITH). The desk marks the war premium a *geopolitics overlay* — "underwrite name-by-name, do not chase" — so the crude price is a reason to look, not a reason to pay.

Archetype guess: `dividend_income_anchor` · method card: VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL (O&G).

**Fast-disqualify checks.** (1) EV at the registry prior (0.60/+25/−15) = **+9.0%** — positive. (2) **Valuation-anchored target not yet established**: no SHEL dossier and an empty inbox, so this session will not open a 20-F to price it. That is the reason this is WATCH and not ADVANCE — the entry has not been tested against a target. (3) Sources would be the 20-F and the quarterly FCF/buyback disclosure; reachable.

**Questions a deep-dive must answer.** What FCF yield does $100.12 imply at the model's own Brent deck, and does it cover the buyback plus dividend at $85 crude? How much of the return is the war premium versus the LNG book? What is the downside if Brent reverts to the band floor near $87?

**Re-test:** ADVANCE only on a target, not on a further rally.
